k: We're playing Catch the Keeper's Girl! You be her! You have to run, and if we catch you, we throw you off the edge!
src: 'We\'re playing Catch the Keeper\'s Girl! You be her! You have to run, and if we catch you, we throw you off the edge!'

k: ...PRETEND off the edge. Kay always cries if it's real off the edge.
src: '...PRETEND off the edge. Kay always cries if it\'s real off the edge.'

k: I don't like that game. I think the Keeper's girl was probably just sad.
src: 'I don\'t like that game. I think the Keeper\'s girl was probably just sad.'

k: Mama says sad people do stupid things. Mama did one once. She married Papa.
src: 'Mama says sad people do stupid things. Mama did one once. She married Papa.'

k: Trader, out of Kiteholm. North, past the wind-stacks. Town of kites and scrap.
src: 'Trader, out of Kiteholm. North, past the wind-stacks. Town of kites and scrap.'

k: A gang of orphans runs the scrap-yards there. Boss is a boy — twelve, maybe. Mouth like a sailor, fingers like a magpie. He took my purse, then gave it back because I "looked like I needed it more."
src: 'A gang of orphans runs the scrap-yards there. Boss is a boy — twelve, maybe. Mouth like a sailor, fingers like a magpie. He took my purse, then gave it back because I "looked like I needed it more."'

k: And a big blond sellsword who drinks too much and cries at sea shanties. Kiteholm's a strange place.
src: 'And a big blond sellsword who drinks too much and cries at sea shanties. Kiteholm\'s a strange place.'

k: I come out here to the edge every morning and I count to a hundred.
src: 'I come out here to the edge every morning and I count to a hundred.'

k: I don't jump. I just count. Then I go back and eat my soup.
src: 'I don\'t jump. I just count. Then I go back and eat my soup.'

k: It's a good number, a hundred. You should try it.
src: 'It\'s a good number, a hundred. You should try it.'

k: Letters, pinned three deep. "MAMA — I'M ON THE BIG ROCK. THERE'S SOUP." "TO WHOEVER HAS MY DOG: HIS NAME IS BISCUIT."
src: 'Letters, pinned three deep. "MAMA — I\'M ON THE BIG ROCK. THERE\'S SOUP." "TO WHOEVER HAS MY DOG: HIS NAME IS BISCUIT."'

k: "DAD — I KEPT THE BOAT. I KEPT IT. COME AND SEE." "To Corporal Hask, if you're alive: I forgive you for the thing with the goat."
src: '"DAD — I KEPT THE BOAT. I KEPT IT. COME AND SEE." "To Corporal Hask, if you\'re alive: I forgive you for the thing with the goat."'

k: Lost Wall
src: 'Lost Wall'

k: Right in the middle of the wall: "Dear Sun." And beside it, a small square of paper signed only "— W."
src: 'Right in the middle of the wall: "Dear Sun." And beside it, a small square of paper signed only "— W."'

k: Hundreds of letters to people nobody can find. The paper rustles in the ash-wind like a flock of birds that cannot quite take off.
src: 'Hundreds of letters to people nobody can find. The paper rustles in the ash-wind like a flock of birds that cannot quite take off.'

k: "Bram — if a girl with red hair asks, tell her I'm sorry I never wrote back." The handwriting is shaky. There's no name.
src: '"Bram — if a girl with red hair asks, tell her I\'m sorry I never wrote back." The handwriting is shaky. There\'s no name.'

k: Maela's kettle. Big enough to bathe a pony in. Always full. Always gray.
src: 'Maela\'s kettle. Big enough to bathe a pony in. Always full. Always gray.'

k: A cot and a cup of something hot. Forty gold. The beds are hammocks. Don't ask what the hammocks used to be.
src: 'A cot and a cup of something hot. Forty gold. The beds are hammocks. Don\'t ask what the hammocks used to be.'

k: the Upturned Keel
src: 'the Upturned Keel'

k: There was a sky-captain through here, back in the spring. Tried to buy a whole barrel of rum on a promise.
src: 'There was a sky-captain through here, back in the spring. Tried to buy a whole barrel of rum on a promise.'

k: Said he had a ship. Said she was grounded at some place called the Roost. Said a lot of things. Sang most of them.
src: 'Said he had a ship. Said she was grounded at some place called the Roost. Said a lot of things. Sang most of them.'

k: We play for ash-potatoes. Stakes are high. Very high. I'm down eleven potatoes.
src: 'We play for ash-potatoes. Stakes are high. Very high. I\'m down eleven potatoes.'

k: Funny. Nothing to buy, and we still gamble.
src: 'Funny. Nothing to buy, and we still gamble.'

k: The bar: a ship's rail laid across two barrels. A brass bell hangs over it. Nobody rings it. Nobody likes bells anymore.
src: 'The bar: a ship\'s rail laid across two barrels. A brass bell hangs over it. Nobody rings it. Nobody likes bells anymore.'

k: A chart of the Shattered Sea, drawn on the back of a sail. Shards marked in charcoal. Most of them have notes: HOUNDS. GLASS. DON'T. One, far to the east, just says: AURENNE? and underneath, smaller: HOSPITAL.
src: 'A chart of the Shattered Sea, drawn on the back of a sail. Shards marked in charcoal. Most of them have notes: HOUNDS. GLASS. DON\'T. One, far to the east, just says: AURENNE? and underneath, smaller: HOSPITAL.'

k: A man asleep under a thin blanket. A gray patch has crept up his neck like frost on a window. Gloam-rot.
src: 'A man asleep under a thin blanket. A gray patch has crept up his neck like frost on a window. Gloam-rot.'

k: Bridge is down. Gods help you.
src: 'Bridge is down. Gods help you.'

k: If you see the Unmoored... don't look it in the eye. It looks back. It remembers things.
src: 'If you see the Unmoored... don\'t look it in the eye. It looks back. It remembers things.'

k: Salvager, once. North spoke's the Chainyard — winch is on the old deck. South spoke's the Psalm — winch is in the deckhouse.
src: 'Salvager, once. North spoke\'s the Chainyard — winch is on the old deck. South spoke\'s the Psalm — winch is in the deckhouse.'

k: Turn both and the strait bridge comes down. I'd do it myself, but I like being alive. It's a habit.
src: 'Turn both and the strait bridge comes down. I\'d do it myself, but I like being alive. It\'s a habit.'

k: Winch
src: 'Winch'

k: Banner
src: 'Banner'

k: The Gilded Psalm's mainmast, snapped off at the deck. Gold leaf still clings to it. The Choir built its ships to be looked at.
src: 'The Gilded Psalm\'s mainmast, snapped off at the deck. Gold leaf still clings to it. The Choir built its ships to be looked at.'

k: A chain-lock as big as a barrel, padlocked to the bridge. The chain runs away north, toward the Chainyard.
src: 'A chain-lock as big as a barrel, padlocked to the bridge. The chain runs away north, toward the Chainyard.'

k: A second chain-lock. This chain runs south, toward the wreck of the Psalm.
src: 'A second chain-lock. This chain runs south, toward the wreck of the Psalm.'

k: ASH SQUARE NOTICESn· Water: one bucket per family. Ask Sorrel.n· Violet under the skin? The Ember Ward. NOW.n· The Undercroft is SEALED. — S.n· BOUNTY: the thing in the Reliquary. See Sorrel.
src:
'ASH SQUARE NOTICES
· Water: one bucket per family. Ask Sorrel.
· Violet under the skin? The Ember Ward. NOW.
· The Undercroft is SEALED. — S.
· BOUNTY: the thing in the Reliquary. See Sorrel.'

k: Ward supply's open, and for once it's got supplies. The Ward Mother's friends pay what it costs. That's the friend discount.
src: 'Ward supply\'s open, and for once it\'s got supplies. The Ward Mother\'s friends pay what it costs. That\'s the friend discount.'

k: Ward supply. Everything costs more than it's worth, because everything's worth more than it costs. Don't think about it too hard.
src: 'Ward supply. Everything costs more than it\'s worth, because everything\'s worth more than it costs. Don\'t think about it too hard.'

k: Soup's got salt in it today. Real salt! Somebody's been generous with somebody.
src: 'Soup\'s got salt in it today. Real salt! Somebody\'s been generous with somebody.'

k: Eat, girl. You've the look of someone who forgets.
src: 'Eat, girl. You\'ve the look of someone who forgets.'

k: Ash soup. Ash bread. Ash, if you're still hungry after.
src: 'Ash soup. Ash bread. Ash, if you\'re still hungry after.'

k: Don't make that face. It's warm, and warm is the only flavor that matters now.
src: 'Don\'t make that face. It\'s warm, and warm is the only flavor that matters now.'

k: Did you HEAR it? It went BONNNG. Osric says he'll teach me to ring it when my arms are long enough.
src: 'Did you HEAR it? It went BONNNG. Osric says he\'ll teach me to ring it when my arms are long enough.'

k: My arms are growing. I checked this morning.
src: 'My arms are growing. I checked this morning.'

k: I'm playing bells. _Tonk. Tonk._ That's a tin can, but you have to pretend.
src: 'I\'m playing bells. _Tonk. Tonk._ That\'s a tin can, but you have to pretend.'

k: Mum says the real bells were so loud you couldn't hear yourself think. I think a lot. I'd like a break.
src: 'Mum says the real bells were so loud you couldn\'t hear yourself think. I think a lot. I\'d like a break.'

k: I was an acolyte. Third Choir, tenor. I wore white.
src: 'I was an acolyte. Third Choir, tenor. I wore white.'

k: I sang the Vespersong that night. Not in the Lantern — just in the nave, with three hundred others. We didn't know. We thought it was a hymn for a long summer.
src: 'I sang the Vespersong that night. Not in the Lantern — just in the nave, with three hundred others. We didn\'t know. We thought it was a hymn for a long summer.'

k: I burned my robes. People here know anyway. They let me carry water. I think that's worse than if they spat.
src: 'I burned my robes. People here know anyway. They let me carry water. I think that\'s worse than if they spat.'

k: I know exactly what he means.
src: 'I know exactly what he means.'

k: Dawnguard. Was. Garrick's lot went up to the Noon Spire with the Hierophant. The rest of us took off our tabards and learned to dig latrines.
src: 'Dawnguard. Was. Garrick\'s lot went up to the Noon Spire with the Hierophant. The rest of us took off our tabards and learned to dig latrines.'

k: Kestrel? Bram Kestrel? The squire who froze at his trial? Ha — I knew him. Big lad. Good lad, for a coward.
src: 'Kestrel? Bram Kestrel? The squire who froze at his trial? Ha — I knew him. Big lad. Good lad, for a coward.'

k: Heard he's swinging a sword for a scrap baron up at Kiteholm now. Heard he drinks. Can't say I blame him.
src: 'Heard he\'s swinging a sword for a scrap baron up at Kiteholm now. Heard he drinks. Can\'t say I blame him.'

k: Jory wants to go to Kiteholm. "There's wind up there," he says. "Wind means weather. Weather means maybe a morning."
src: 'Jory wants to go to Kiteholm. "There\'s wind up there," he says. "Wind means weather. Weather means maybe a morning."'

k: I told him there are no mornings anymore. He said that's what everybody said about the bells.
src: 'I told him there are no mornings anymore. He said that\'s what everybody said about the bells.'

k: Ada thinks I'm a dreamer. Ada married a dreamer. Ada should've read the label.
src: 'Ada thinks I\'m a dreamer. Ada married a dreamer. Ada should\'ve read the label.'

k: If the Ward Mother can make medicine out of a flooded hole, I can find a morning on a kite.
src: 'If the Ward Mother can make medicine out of a flooded hole, I can find a morning on a kite.'

k: My husband was on the far side of the bridge when the city broke away.
src: 'My husband was on the far side of the bridge when the city broke away.'

k: I come every evening. It's always evening. So I'm always here.
src: 'I come every evening. It\'s always evening. So I\'m always here.'

k: Our Ward Mother, going below? With _you_?
src: 'Our Ward Mother, going below? With _you_?'

k: Then you'd better bring her back, or there's an old woman in Ash Square who will learn to swing a poker.
src: 'Then you\'d better bring her back, or there\'s an old woman in Ash Square who will learn to swing a poker.'

k: Come sit by the fire, girl. I tell the children stories so they don't ask questions.
src: 'Come sit by the fire, girl. I tell the children stories so they don\'t ask questions.'

k: Once upon a time, the sun came up every morning. They don't believe me. Neither do I, some days.
src: 'Once upon a time, the sun came up every morning. They don\'t believe me. Neither do I, some days.'
